actions.name: compromise routers and install AVrecon malware
actions.description: Threat actors have been found to compromise routers, install AVrecon malware, and then sell access to the compromised devices as residential proxies using the SocksEscort residential proxy service.

actions.name: exploit known vulnerabilities in routers and IOT devices
actions.description: SocksEscort threat actors have exploited known vulnerabilities in various routers and IOT devices to gain access to the devices and install AVrecon malware.

actions.name: use AVrecon malware to maintain remote access and use infected routers as part of a botnet
actions.description: AVrecon malware allows SocksEscort threat actors to maintain remote access to the routers and use them as part of a botnet.

actions.name: sell access to compromised devices as residential proxies under SocksEscort brand
actions.description: SocksEscort monetizes their botnet through various illicit methods, including selling access under the SocksEscort residential proxy brand.

actions.name: update AVrecon stored configuration
actions.description: AVrecon can update its stored configuration.

actions.name: establish remote shell to attacker-controlled server
actions.description: AVrecon can establish a remote shell to an attacker-controlled server.

actions.name: download and execute arbitrary payloads using AVrecon as a loader
actions.description: AVrecon acts as a loader by downloading and executing arbitrary payloads.

actions.name: infect small-office/home-office (SOHO) routers using critical vulnerabilities such as RCE and command injection
actions.description: The vast majority of observed devices infected with AVrecon malware are small-office/home-office (SOHO) routers infected using critical vulnerabilities such as Remote Code Execution (RCE) and command injection.

actions.name: execute loader first to test environment and check if AVrecon is running before deploying AVrecon
actions.description: On certain models, a loader is executed first to test the environment and check to see if AVrecon is already running, before downloading and deploying AVrecon.

actions.name: persist AVrecon by flashing device with custom firmware containing AVrecon
actions.description: Threat actors utilize a device’s built-in update features to flash the device with a custom firmware image containing AVrecon, hardcoded to execute AVrecon on device startup.

actions.name: modify firmware to disable device’s update and flashing features
actions.description: Threat actors modify the firmware to silently disable the device’s update and flashing features, making AVrecon extremely difficult to remove.

actions.name: deploy AVrecon without persistence mechanism on some devices
actions.description: In some cases, AVrecon is deployed without a persistence mechanism; if an infected device is power cycled, it resets to a normal state and is no longer infected.

actions.name: remotely re-infect devices after power cycling using same known vulnerabilities
actions.description: AVrecon C2 servers reacted to the loss of an infected device by remotely re-infecting it with the same known vulnerabilities used to initially infect the device.

actions.name: infected routers communicate with SocksEscort C2 servers over ports 8080 and 8000
actions.description: Infected routers have been observed communicating with SocksEscort C2 servers over port 8080 and 8000.

actions.name: exchange PING and PONG messages every 60 seconds between AVrecon and C2 server
actions.description: AVrecon malware prompts the infected device to communicate with its designated C2 server over port 8000 every 60 seconds using a custom loop in which AVrecon and the C2 server exchange the words “PING” and “PONG” until the C2 has a command for AVrecon to execute.

actions.name: open tunnel to SocksEscort relay server upon C2 command
actions.description: The C2 may interrupt the “PING/PONG” loop to direct the router to open a tunnel to a SocksEscort relay server.

actions.name: use SocksEscort relay servers to enable customers to tunnel traffic through infected routers
actions.description: SocksEscort relay servers enable SocksEscort customers to connect and tunnel their traffic through residential routers infected with AVrecon.
